```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 8, fig.height = 5, dpi = 90, message = FALSE)
has_mvln <- requireNamespace("mvtnorm", quietly = TRUE) && requireNamespace("MASS", quietly = TRUE)
has_ss3diags <- requireNamespace("ss3diags", quietly = TRUE)
library(ss3diags2)
library(ggplot2)
```

`ss3diags2` extracts observations and outputs of Stock Synthesis (SS3) models, read with `r4ss::SS_output()`, into
long `data.table` tables that convert to FLR objects (`FLQuants`, `FLIndices`, `FLStockR`, `FLPar`), and plots them
with `ggplot2`. Inputs are shaped for JABBA3 and FLicc. This guide shows the functionality on `ss3simple`, the
simulated "simple_small" model of r4ss. It is the example used by the PIFSC version of ss3diags
(<https://github.com/PIFSCstockassessments/ss3diags>), so results can be compared directly. A second vignette,
*Season-, sex- and area-structured models*, applies the tools to the northern shrimp assessment (four seasons,
hermaphrodite, two areas, six area-specific fleets).

| ss3diags                     | ss3diags2                                              |
|------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------|
| `SSplotRunstest()`, `SSrunstest()` | `ss3_runs()`, `ss3plot_runs()` (indices, mean length, mean age) |
| `SSplotJABBAres()`, `SSrmse()` | `ss3plot_jres()`                                      |
| `SSplotRetro()`, `SShcbias()`  | `ss3_retro()`, `ss3_mohn()`, `ss3plot_retro()`        |
| `SSplotHCxval()`, `SSmase()`   | `ss3_hindcast()`, `ss3plot_hcxval()`                  |
| `SSdeltaMVLN()`, `SSplotKobe()` | `ss3mvln()`, `ss3stk()`, `ss3plot_trj()`, `ss3plot_kobe()` |
| (Pearson residuals in r4ss)  | `ss3_resid()` (OSA), `ss3plot_resid()`                 |

# 1. Fleets and observations

```{r obs}
data(ss3simple)
ss3_fleets(ss3simple)
ct  <- ss3_catch(ss3simple)                  # FLQuants by fleet
idx <- ss3_indices(ss3simple)                # FLIndices of FLIndexBiomass, input SE in index.var
lfd <- ss3_lencomp(ss3simple)                # FLQuants by fleet, sex as unit
afd <- ss3_agecomp(ss3simple)
ss3plot_data(catch = ct, indices = idx, lencomp = lfd, agecomp = afd)
```

Each extractor has `what = "exp"` for the model fit, which the plots overlay:

```{r fits}
ss3plot_indices(idx, fit = ss3_indices(ss3simple, what = "exp"))
ss3plot_comps(lfd, fit = ss3_lencomp(ss3simple, what = "exp"), by = "unit")
ss3plot_comps(afd, type = "bubble", by = "unit")
```

`ss2jabba3()` and `ss2flicc()` return the same observations shaped as JABBA3 and FLicc inputs (catch in weight by
fleet, annual indices with input SEs; length compositions by gear on common bins and years).

# 2. Life history and growth

`ss3_lhpar()` returns an `FLPar` of growth, maturity, length-weight and M by sex (unit), the FLicc `lhpar`. Growth
curves by sex can be overlaid on the length compositions as ridges, observed and expected, with cohort tracks.

```{r growth}
lh <- ss3_lhpar(ss3simple)
lh
ss3plot_growth(ss3simple, lfd = lfd)
```

```{r ridges, fig.height = 7}
ss3plot_ridges(lfd, fit = ss3_lencomp(ss3simple, what = "exp"), type = "both", fleets = "SURVEY1", lhpar = lh)
```

# 3. Residual diagnostics

One-step-ahead (OSA) residuals follow the SS3 likelihood (multinomial, or Dirichlet-multinomial with the precision
implied by the SS3 effective sample size; Trijoulet et al. 2023). Cohort tracks of von Bertalanffy growth by sex
help to see year classes. `fleets =` and `units =` select panels.

```{r osa, fig.height = 6}
rl <- ss3_resid(ss3simple)                   # length
ss3plot_resid(rl, lhpar = lh)
ss3plot_resid(ss3_resid(ss3simple, "age"), units = "F")
ss3plot_resid(rl, type = "qq")
```

OSA residuals are conditional on the smaller bins: too few small fish gives negative residuals at small lengths
and positive residuals at larger lengths.

Runs tests on the log residuals of the indices (or of mean length or age) with 3-sigma limits, and the joint
residual plot:

```{r runs}
ss3_runs(ss3simple)
ss3plot_runs(ss3simple)
ss3plot_runs(ss3simple, quant = "len")
ss3plot_jres(ss3simple)
```

Retrospective analysis and hindcast cross-validation need a set of SS3 runs with peels, read with
`r4ss::SSgetoutput()` and `r4ss::SSsummarize()`:

```{r retro, eval = has_ss3diags}
data(natl.sma, package = "ss3diags")         # retro.sma: shortfin mako peels
rt <- ss3_retro(retro.sma)
ss3_mohn(rt, quants = c("SSB", "F"))
ss3plot_retro(rt, type = c("SSB", "F"))
hc <- ss3_hindcast(retro.sma)
hc$mase
ss3plot_hcxval(hc)
```

# 4. Stock status: FLStockR and MVLN

`ss3stk()` builds the simplified `FLStockR` of `FLRef::ss2FLStockR()`: maximum likelihood estimates with standard
errors (`output = "mle"`), or draws from a multivariate lognormal (MVLN) approximation (`output = "iters"`,
`ss3mvln()`).

* `ss3mvln(method = "joint")` (default) draws SSB, recruitment and F of all years and the reference points from one
  MVLN with the full correlation matrix of the SS3 derived quantities (Kell et al. 2023; the `ss3om::ssmvln()`
  approach). Each iteration is a coherent trajectory and the reference points have iterations.
* `ss3mvln(method = "annual")` is the delta-MVLN of `ss3diags::SSdeltaMVLN()` (Walter and Winker 2020;
  Winker et al. 2019), drawn year by year.

```{r mvln, eval = has_mvln, fig.height = 7}
stk <- ss3stk(ss3simple, output = "iters", iters = 500, fwd = TRUE)
ss3plot_trj(stk)
```

**Note on SSdeltaMVLN.** For the example models the year-by-year delta-MVLN understates the correlation between
B/Bmsy and F/Fmsy in the terminal year (shortfin mako: -0.24, against -0.86 in the SS3 covariance; Pacific hake:
-0.26 against -0.76), so its Kobe clouds are rounder than the estimated uncertainty. The joint method keeps the
estimated correlation. Use `method = "joint"` for advice.

# 5. Kobe plots and the timing of F and SSB  {#kobe-lag}

> **Critical for advice.** SS3 reports SSB at spawning (typically at the start of the year), and F of year *y* acts
> during year *y*. The SSB that results from the fishing in year *y* is therefore SSB in year *y + 1*. The usual Kobe
> plot pairs F(*y*) with SSB(*y*): it shows the biomass the fishery in *y* started from, not the biomass it led to.
> When F is well above Fmsy, the stock status that follows from the current exploitation can be markedly worse
> than the plot of F(*y*) against SSB(*y*) suggests. Advice should state which convention is used and, when the
> two differ, show both.

`ss3plot_kobe(lag = 1)` plots F(*y*) against B/Btgt(*y + 1*). The uncertainty cloud then pairs F(*Y*) with B(*Y + 1*)
within each iteration, which needs draws linked across years: use `ss3mvln(method = "joint")` (a warning is given for
year-by-year draws). Build the stock with `fwd = TRUE` so that SSB at the start of the year after the last assessment
year (reported by SS3 as a forecast quantity) is available; F is used up to the end year only.

```{r kobe, eval = has_mvln, fig.width = 11, fig.height = 4.5}
k0 <- ss3plot_kobe(stk) + ggtitle("lag = 0: F(y) against B(y)")
k1 <- ss3plot_kobe(stk, lag = 1) + ggtitle("lag = 1: F(y) against B(y + 1)")
if(requireNamespace("patchwork", quietly = TRUE)) patchwork::wrap_plots(k0, k1) else k1
```

For North Atlantic shortfin mako the probability of being overfished and subject to overfishing (red quadrant) in
2015 is about 78% with F(2015) against SSB(2015) and about 93% with F(2015) against SSB(2016).

Points to check before using the lagged plot for advice:

* SSB(*y + 1*) for the last assessment year is a one-year forecast: it depends on the SS3 forecast settings
  (`forecast.ss`) and, where recruits mature within a year, on the forecast recruitment.
* Kell et al. (2023) pair F and SSB both ways in their figures (F in 2020 with SSB in 2021, and both in 2022); the
  convention is not standardised, which is why it must be stated with the advice.

# 6. Production function and equilibrium

`ss3_spm()` fits a Pella-Tomlinson production function to the SS3 equilibrium yield curve and checks it against
the SS3 benchmarks. SS3 holds several "unfished" states: SSB_Virgin (start-year biology), SSB_unfished (benchmark
years) and the dynamic B0 of each year; with time-varying weight-at-age or M (empirical `wtatage`) these differ, and
the equilibrium table can rest on yet another biology. `ss3_spm()` warns when its fit and the SS3 benchmarks differ.

```{r spm}
stk1 <- ss3stk(ss3simple)
ss3plot_production(stk1)
```

# 7. Selectivity, recruitment and fishing mortality

```{r sel}
ss3plot_sel(ss3_sel(ss3simple))
ss3plot_sr(ss3simple)
ss3plot_fa(ss3_fa(ss3simple))                # F-at-age by fleet (and season)
```

`ss3_partialF()` splits F among fleets or groups of fleets and `ss3_impact()` gives the loss of SSB caused by each
group after Wang et al. (2009), both from the SS3 report without re-running SS3. With one fishery the impact is
simply the dynamic B0 minus SSB; the projection without fishing reproduces the SS3 dynamic B0
(`ss3simple$Dynamic_Bzero`), which checks the method:

```{r impact}
imp <- ss3_impact(ss3simple)
imp
ss3plot_impact(imp)
```

The vignette *Season-, sex- and area-structured models* shows partial F, F by area and the impact of fleet groups
for the northern shrimp assessment.

Trijoulet, V., Albertsen, C.M., Kristensen, K., Legault, C.M., Miller, T.J. and Nielsen, A. (2023). Model validation
for compositional data in stock assessment models: calculating residuals with correct properties. Fisheries
Research, 257: 106487.

Walter, J. and Winker, H. (2020). Projections to create Kobe 2 Strategy Matrix using the multivariate log-normal
approximation for Atlantic yellowfin tuna. ICCAT SCRS/2019/145.
